Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:

History of Present Illness:
Mr. ___ is a ___ gentleman with a history of myeloma 
admitted for high dose Cytoxan and stem cell mobilization.  The 
patient has been treated with Revlimid and Decadron with 
excellent response.  
.
Of note, the patient had a history of weight loss of unclear 
etiology, thought most likely to be due to depression and 
alcohol intake.  The patient has been seen by psychiatry, was 
started on antidepressants and had significantly improved over 
time. However, the plan is to discontinue citalopram prior to 
his transplant.   
.
In terms of workup for his transplant cardiac workup, the 
patient has a AAA; he has been evaluated by cardiology and there 
is no immediate need for surgical repair. Over the past week, 
the patient has noticed new, nonpainful bilateral lower 
extremity foot swelling of unclear etiology. It symmetrical 
initially, but when he was seen in clinic several days ago was 
improving in the RLE with persistence in the LLE.  He denies 
SOB, orthopnea, DOE.  BLE LENIs are negative.  Repeat ECHO shows 
an intact ejection fraction.  He has no history of heart 
failure.  In terms of workup for his transplant pulmonary 
workup, the patient has a decreased lung function at baseline 
due to history of multilobar pneumonia and smoking; DLCO now 
shows DLCO of slightly greater than 50%, which meets criteria 
for going forward.  
.
He was recently admitted to the ___ unit on ___ with right 
knee cellulitis.  He was initially treated with IV Vancomycin 
and transitioned to PO Keflex prior to discharge.  He has had no 
recurrent symptoms of right knee cellulitis
